questions.q: What are the names of Salesforce's three annual releases, in order?
options: Spring, Summer, Winter
Winter, Spring, Fall
Alpha, Beta, General Availability
questions.explain: Salesforce ships three major releases a year named for their launch season: Spring (around February), Summer (around June), and Winter (around October, numbered for the following year).

questions.q: Why do Sandbox orgs receive a new release before Production orgs do?
options: Because Sandboxes are physically located on faster servers
So admins, developers, and QA teams can test the release against their own customizations before it reaches live, customer-facing data
Because Sandbox orgs are optional and rarely used
Because Production orgs never receive release upgrades
questions.explain: The Sandbox preview window exists specifically so teams can test the upcoming release safely before it reaches Production — catching any regressions ahead of time.

questions.q: How does a Production org actually receive a new Salesforce release?
options: Each user individually downloads and installs the new release
The company must pay an additional fee to receive the upgrade
An admin must manually click an 'Install Release' button in Setup
It upgrades automatically during a scheduled maintenance window tied to its instance
questions.explain: Because Salesforce is multitenant, there's no manual install step — Production orgs upgrade automatically during a scheduled maintenance window published per instance on trust.salesforce.com.

questions.q: What does it mean when a new feature is described as 'opt-in' after a release?
options: The feature was removed from the release at the last minute
The feature only works for Developer Edition orgs
The feature exists in the org but is off by default until an admin deliberately enables it
The feature is permanently unavailable to that org
questions.explain: Opt-in features exist after the release but stay off by default, so admins can choose when to turn them on rather than having behavior change without warning.

questions.q: Why would a working Salesforce admin pay attention to release notes on an ongoing basis?
options: Admins are legally required to memorize every release note
Release notes replace the need for Setup entirely
Release notes are only relevant to Salesforce's own engineering staff
To catch new declarative tools, understand any behavior changes, and because certifications require periodic release-specific maintenance modules
questions.explain: Release notes matter for spotting regression risk, discovering useful new declarative features, and maintaining Salesforce certifications, which require passing release-specific maintenance modules a few times a year.
